articleTitle: Ferrites as radiating & receiving microelements in the frequengy range of 23 MHz to 450 MHz
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Investigations are always going on by various worker towards size reductions of antennas for different frequency ranges. During the recent past a number of developments have been made a the field of magnetic materials (1). Though these materials cover a wide range of working frequencies starting from 25 MHz to as high as microwave frequencies for various applications, the advantages of the same were not considered earlier for being used in radiating elements in the VHF range. This paper deals with one such investigation where the advantage of using ferrimagnetic materials as substrate element for strip antennas has been considered. Towards this inference, a number of Lithium Chromium Titanium vanadium ferrite have been developed in laboratory scales whose permeabilities and permittivities are very much suited for being used as substrate elements for strip antennas are the VHF range. These antennas are very simple in shape, light in weight with added advantages of having higher band widths and omnidirectional pattern.

articleTitle: Research activities in photonics at the national optics institute
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The National Optics Institute (NOI) was incorporated on December 13, 1985, as a non-profit organization. The goal of this organization is to provide the Canadian optics industry with the support for research and development (R&D) and the technical assistance necessary to its growth. The Institute is currently working in three principal sectors, namely: lasers and their applications, opto-electronics (including optical communication), special optic elements and normalization and calibration.

articleTitle: Practical MMIC design approaches for phased array antenna elements
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Phased array antennas have been receiving considerable attention in the 1930's due to the rapid evolution of monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMIC). The requirements for phased arrays differ considerable depending on whether they are for radars or for communications and whether they are to be airborne, space-based, or terrestrially located. However, in general, the basic elements include phase shifters and amplifiers. There have been a number of papers published on GaAs MMIC amplifiers and phase shifters. [1,2]. However, these papers have not addressed the design approaches necessary to insure that the MMIC meets its required specifications.

articleTitle: Beam scanning properties of circular array of anisotropic cylinders
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Eggimann [1] has suggested that a circular array of ferrite cylinders surrounding an electric line source might shift its main lobe by varying the applied magnetic field. Later, Okamoto [2] presented a numerical method for solving the two dimensional problem of scattering by multiple gyrotropic cylinders. He then showed by numerical results the possibility of beam scanning by a circular array of plasma cylinders [3]. He also designed and investigated the performance of a scanning antenna using ferrite rods [4]. He found that the pattern of this antenna has a beam with suppressed sidelobes. However, in Okamoto's work the main lobe could be rotated only at intervals of about 30° by gradually changing the axial magnetic field applied to the respective ferrites, and, a continuous scanning could not be achieved.

articleTitle: On the frequency stability of dielectric resonators
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A typical dielectric resonator structure with shielded walls is considered and the various physical parameters have been varied to see their effects on the frequency stability. These parameters are of importance for investigations, since, in many applications, the dielectric resonators are exposed to different environmental conditions and as such it is important to know the effects of such changes on the frequency stability.

articleTitle: Near-field scattering of a conducting sphere irradiated by a dipole
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The near-scattered field of a perfectly coducting sphere located in the far-field of a dipole, is investigated. In the case which is presented here, the size of the sphere is of the order of the wavelength or greater, for which the plane wave illumination approximation is not valid. Numerical approaches, based on the moment method, have shown instabilities in field computations for observation points located at fractions of wavelength from the scat t erer. Measurements performed in an anechoic chamber confirmed that the oscillatory nature of the numerical results were due to numercial instabilities. Using the assumption that the field produced by the half-wave dipole on the surface of the sphere is a spherical wave, and analytical closed-form solution using a spherical eigen-mode expansion is proposed and compared with numerical and experimental results. It was found that the results corroborate the instability nature of the numerical method for very near locations of the observation points to the scatterer.

articleTitle: Experiments on a detector array for real-time location of buried objects
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Experiment· were conducted to measure the response characteristic· of a detector system consisting of an array of two electromagnetic pulse induction tensor·. Laboratory data for three object : (1)a ıteel sphere (2) a steel prolate spheroid and (3) an 81 mm mortar casing are presented in order to discuss how the response of an object varies with its depth, orientation and lateral offset from coil centres. Relevance of these result· to developing algorithms for location of metallic objects are also pointed out. Finally, data obtained from a scan over buried targets are presented to illustrate a practical application.

articleTitle: Random noise bursts: Observations and mitigation in s-band telemetry, tracking & command antenna feed
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The generation of Intermodulation interference by nonlinear conduction mechanisms in normally passive hardware components can lead to severe degradation in the performance of muiticarrier communication systems in satellites, space probes and ground-based systems. If a common path for closely-spaced high power transmit and sensitive receive bands can not be avoided in the system, it is very difficult to ensure that the passive nonlinear behaviour resulting in noise bursts or Intermodulation generation will be well below the desired level. Electron tunnelling through Aluminium Oxide films on aluminium structures, and waveguide flanges, surface finish, workmanship etc. have been found to be responsible for such phenomenon.

articleTitle: Radar cross sections for two conducting spheroids of arbitrary orientation
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Bistatic and backscattering cross sections associated with the field scattered by two perfectly conducting prolate spheroids of arbitrary orientation, are calculated for an arbitrary polarization and direction of propagation of the incident, uniform plane electromagnetic wave. Numerical results are presented for spheroids with various axial ratios and orientations.

articleTitle: Numerical problems in reconstruction of a dielectric object from its scattered electric field
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: When using the method of moments to solve an opeator equation, the stability of the system of linear equations resulting from the discretization process should be noted. This can be done by computing the κ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> condition number using public domain FORTRAN code such as LINPACK.

articleTitle: The dyadic green's functions in both hollow and loaded rectangular waveguides and it's applications
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Waveguide obstacles are long standing problems in electromagnetical theory[1], due to the deficiencies of the Dyadic Green's function (DOF) in the waveguide regionas.

articleTitle: Architecture for active antennas using MMIC devices
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The maturing of MMIC technology opens up many interesting options in the design of ground and space segment antennas. Using MMIC components in direct radiating arrays or array fed reflector antennas makes it possible to implement multiple beams and reconfigurability that would be impractical to implement using a passive array. Distribution of amplification implies transmit beam forming at low power levels, permitting higher losses and therefore greater complexity in the beam forming network. In the receive function, distributed amplification is advantageous as losses occuring after amplification won't significantly degrade signal to noise (S/N) ratio.

articleTitle: Application of numerical methods in electromagnetic wave well-logging problems
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The introduction of numerical methods in Electromagnetic Theory has solved, a number of problems which conventional or analytical methods failed. Electromagnetic wave well-logging is an important application of Electromagnetics. As EM waves penetrate the stratified media, the phase difference and amplitude ratio which well-logging tool measures vary [1]. FEM [2] and BEM [3] are applied to the simulation of Radio-frequenoy well-logging curve in this paper to enhance the numerical methods of well-logging analysis. A memory-saving FEM algorithm is derived and programmed. The results are in good agreement with those obtained by other methods. For stratified and inhomogeneous media FEN grid varies little, so the cpu time and storage required are about the same. This is the disadvantage of FEU. BEM can be used to treat the stratified case specifically and the numerical solutions are acceptable compared with analytic solutions. [8].

articleTitle: MMIC based future generation MLS phase-array antennas
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Microwave Landing System<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup> (MLS) is a new standard system endorsed by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) to replace Instrument Landing Systems (ILS) now in general use. MLS operates at C-Band which permits ranges up to 30 nautical miles to be reliably achieved with modest transmitting powers. With MLS's, ground transmitters provide signals that can be decoded in an aircraft to determine both range, and azimuth and elevation angles of approach. The information is time-multiplexed with additional digital data to provide information such as airport and runway identification, wind vectors, site data, system status, and other operational details.

articleTitle: Low loss continuously variable WIC phase shifter for MLS antenna
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A wide-band continuously variable phase shifter for Microwave Landing System (MLS) providing 90 degrees phase shift at 5.1 GHz was designed using MMIC technology. The basic configuration is a distributed loaded line using reverse biased Schottky diodes as varactors. Return loss should be in excess of 20 dB over the required MLS bandwidth ensuring excellent coscadobllity. Mean Insertion loss of 0.6 dB with 0.2 dB maximum variation is also expected. Phase setting and tuning is done using a single low current analog bios. Four chips can be cascaded to yield 360 degree phase control using a single analog bias. The 1 × 2 mm circuit should operate from 1 to 12 GHz with linear phase shift with frequency and return loss in excess of 15 dB.

articleTitle: Eigenvalues of nonzero-integer order spherical wave functions of coaxial and biconical structures
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Accurate eigenvalues of nonzero-integer spherical wave functions of coaxial and biconical structures are determined for both TE and TM fields. It is found that the number of the eigenvalues is equal to the order of the characteristic equations, i.e., the order of the related associated Legendre functions and their derivatives. For each TE mode there is a unique nontrivial eigenvalue, which is the degree of the coherent associated Legendre function, larger than m − 1/2 (m is the order of the characteristic equation). For the TM modes, nontrivial eigenvalues do not exist. All eigenvalues are integer and less than the order m, which are trivial solutions for practical problems.

articleTitle: Use of touchstone in the design and analysis of microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Use of commercially available TOUCHSTONE software package for the analysis and design of microstrip patch antennas is investigated. It turns out that the resonant frequency of a rectangular patch can be accurately computed by treating the patch as a transmission line loaded at both ends with an open-circuit capacitance and a radiation conductance.

articleTitle: Design and realization of a passive and active 3-branch optical power divider/switch in Ti:LiNbO3
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Passive and active y-junction dielectric waveguides have been the subject of extensive theoretical and experimental investigations, in view of their potential applications as power dividers, switches, modulators, TE-TM mode splitters etc. in integrated optical circuits. However, multibranch waveguides with more than two branches have received much less attention.

articleTitle: Scattering of electromagnetic waves by cylinders of different kinds
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The scattering by infinitely long cylinders is a classical two-dimensional electromagnetic problem that can, in principle, be solved numerically. Mei and Van Bladel [1] have formulated the problem for a conducting cylinder of arbitrary cross-section using integral equation formulations. They have then reduced these integral equations to a matrix equation to determine the surface currents, which are subsequently used to calculate the far scattered fields. Banough and Goldsmith [2] have also used an integral equation approach to handle the scattering by arbitrary shaped cylinders. These formulations are general and can also be used to study the scattering by multiple cylinders. However, they provide numerical results for the surface currents and far fields and fail to provide an analytic form for the solution to help understanding the scattering properties. On the other hand, for investigating the scattering by conducting cylinders of arbitrary shape Mullin et al [3] have introduced a method that determines directly the scattering functions of the object. It is therefore more useful for understanding the scattering properties and the convergence of the solution.

articleTitle: Early-time current response of a circular cylinder excited by a unit-step line source
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Early-time current response of a conducting cylinder to a step-function electromagnetic plane wave has been already thoroughly studied [l]-[4]. In this paper, we consider the early-time response of a perfectly conducting circular cylinder to cylindrical electromagnetic waves generated by a parallel filament carrying a unit-step current. The geometry of the problem is shown in Fig. 1. The mathematical technique utilized in this paper is different from that in our previous work [5], where the Watson transformation is employed to obtain the solution for the shadow region and the physical optics approximation for the illuminated region. The new approach consists in applying a double Laplace transform of the wave equation for the vector potential with respect to time and angle. From the solution of the ordinary differential equation satisfied by the transformed vector potential, the transformed current density induced on the surface of the cylinder is derived. To obtain the real time surface current density we perform first the inversion of the angle transform for large values of the time transform variable, by using the theorem of residues for the shadow region and the saddle point technique for the illuminated region. A second inverse Laplace transform yields the time dependent early-time solution.

articleTitle: Transient behavior of scanning antenna with elliptical aperture
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In many modern applications the use of antennas of huge dimensions and time pulses of very short duration creates a situation where the transient behavior is of practical importance. The transient behavior of aperture antennas has been studied by Polk [1]. The formula derived by him is based on the frequency spectrum method of analysis. But as D. K. Cheng and F. I. Tseng pointed out [2], the formula is difficult to be used. Recently, a new analytical method in time domain was proposed by S. M. Lin for the case of rectangular aperture [4].

articleTitle: Radiation from conical reflectors with a dipole array feed
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The radiation characteristics of conical reflectors with a line source feed in the form of an array of dipoles are derived using a numerical integration of the physical optics currents. Representative radiation patterns are computed and presented.

articleTitle: Scattering by a dielectric loaded conducting strip
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper we present a solution to the scattering problem of an E-polarized incident wave on a perfectly conducting strip loaded by a dielectric cylinder. The solution is based on the application of the vector Green's theorem. The numerical results are in good agreement with those based on the method of moments. The dependence of the scattered field as well as the scattering cross-section of the loaded strip on the strip width, dielectric constant and the angle of the incident wave are investigated.

articleTitle: Scattering of dielectric cylinders using a time domain approach
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In recent years, time-domain analysis has received much attention with the importance of transient analysis mainly in EMC/I problems. If one restricts to arbitrary geometries, numerical methods are obviously the most appropriate. Moment-method (MoM) [1] was first applied to the scattering of inhomogeneous objects with arbitrary shape, in both frequency and time domains. This method requires some mathematical preamble which is rather involved. However, it has the advantage of employing a minimum number of unknowns since, by using an integral equation approach, the scatterer only has to be subsectioned rather than the all space. As a result, there is no need for imposing artificial boundary conditions. On the other hand, simpler methods such as finite-difference time-domain technique (FT-DT) and, more recently, transmission-line matrix method (TLM) have been proposed for open field problems [2,3]. Both methods are mathematically less involved but suffer from the fact that, since the all space must be subsectioned, artificial boundary conditions must be imposed to give a limit to the size of the problem. There are some difficulties if these boundaries are not located where field values or expressions are known, in which case the conditions become rather involved and complicate the algorithm. However, both methods can handle nonlinear, time-varying and even, under certain conditions, nonisotropic problems with relatively little mathematical complications.

articleTitle: The characteristic of linear antenna with resistive loading
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Recent study related to electromagnetic-pulse (IMP) and electromagnetic interference (EMI) has caused a strong need to develop an isotropic broadband antenna. One such antenna, which, has been used, is a dipole with, tapered resistive loading in order to support traveling wave on antenna. [11]

articleTitle: Optimal shaped beam reflector antenna design
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: For some antenna applications, radiation is required to be of narrow beam in one plane and to conform to a specified shape in the perpendicular plane. A common example of such an antenna is found in airborne navigational systems which require a cosecant-squared elevation radiation pattern and a narrow beam azimuth pattern.

articleTitle: A phased array microstrip antenna for use on a remotely piloted vehicle
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The design of a phased array microatrip antenna for use on a remotely piloted vehicle it presented. The antenna consists of a 3 × 8 array of circular patch microstrip antenna which operate in the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> modea. The antenna has a fixed elevation pattern and is capable of being steered in aximuth over nearly ±90°. The performance of the array is compared to the performance of a similarly sized array consisting of elements operating in the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode only. A 3 × 1 section of the array was fabricated and tested to validate the design model.

articleTitle: The AC resistance and the current distribution of a low loss microstripline
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In an MMIC (Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit), the dominant loss of the structure can be mainly attributed to the finite conductivity of its microstriplines. A typical microstripline as shown in figure 1 is formed by a rectangular strip conductor located on top of a grounded substrate.

articleTitle: Adaptation of a Ku-band microwave scatterometer for polarimetry measurements of crop canopy
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The adaptation to a polarimeter of a dual polarized, Ku-band, continuous wave, frequency modulated, microwave scatterometer is described. Polarimetry measurements for a field of hard red spring wheat show that the polarized component of the backscattered radiation differs only slightly from the polarization of the illuminating radiation but that the unpolarized backscattered radiation depends on incidence angle and is sensitive to the polarization of the trasmitted signal.

articleTitle: Inflection point caustic problems and solutions for high-gain dual-shaped reflectors
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The GTD diffraction analysis of dual-shaped reflectors<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,2</sup> that are synthesized for high gain and low spillover past the subreflector can lead to erroneous results. The errors are particularly significant for the fields computed in the vicinity of the edge of the main reflector. Thus the computation of spillover energy past the main reflector and the noise figure of the high-gain system can be in error.

articleTitle: Voltage distribution in the aperture of a narrow slot antenna
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An efficient method is introduced for numerical solution of the integral equation for the voltage distribution in a narrow slot. The method of moments is employed to reduce the integral equation to a matrix equation and the Fourier transform technique is applied to eliminate the derivatives in the integrand and to remove the singularity of the kernel. The voltage distribution in the slot and the circuit parameters such as input impedance, resonance frequency and bandwidth are presented for typical examples.

articleTitle: A modulated waveguide slot arry antenna
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The waveguide-fed slot array antenna has created wide interest due to its compactness, light weight and simple series feeding mechanism. Due to its advantages, the SAR and SLAR antennas have been configured using waveguide-fed slot array antenna as a basic element having either Longitudinal slots cut on the broad wall of the waveguide or inclined slot on the narrow wall of the waveguide. Till now, the design and analysis techniques are available for narrow beam generation using waveguide-fed slot array antenna[1]. Very few studies have been made on the realisation of other beam shapes using these antennas[2]. In this paper a new method of generation of various beam shapes by changing the interslot distance of waveguide-fed slot array antenna is presented.

articleTitle: Currrent developments in GPS antenna technology
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents a discussion on current developments in the design and manufacture of Global Positioning System (GPS) antennas at Chu Associates Inc. The primary focus will be the description of different antenna profiles, broadband characteristics, pattern coverage, axial ratio and VSHR. Consideration will also be given to antenna suitability for use in normal or high accuracy positioning systems. Since GPS antenna radiation and profile characteristics will ultimately be decided by the user community, whose requirements vary, a variety of GPS antenna types will be considered.

articleTitle: Scattering by a dielectric coated conducting elliptic cylinder
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An exact treatment using the boundary value method for solving the problem of scattering of a line source field or a plane wave by a perfectly conducting elliptic cylinder coated by a confocal dielectric elliptical shell is presented. For the line source excitation the total field is calculated, while for the plane wave excitation the echo width is obtained. Sample and interesting results for the backscattering echo width versus different geometrical parameters are obtained and presented. A set of design type curves which are useful for locating the maximum or minimum backscattering echo width are also provided.

articleTitle: The radiation characteristics of azimuthal modes on an infinitely long dielectric cylinder
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The radiation characteristics of cos nφ δ(z) current distributions on an infinitely long dielectric circular cylinder are investigated. Exact analytical solutions are presented for the fields resulting from such distributions. Numerical results obtained from the far field approximations to the exact solutions are given. The numerical results clearly indicate the effect of changes in the cylinder's dielectric constant upon the radiation characteristics of the structure.

articleTitle: Shaped-beam planar antenna using microstrip antenna with open-circuited stub
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, a new type of planar shaped-beam antenna using parasitic patches with open stripline-stub was presented and tested in S-band. The desired pattern shown in Fig. 1 can be performed by regulating the length of open stripline-stub.

articleTitle: Comparison of active phased array antennas for communication satellite applications
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The overall performances of a Direct Radiating Array and of a Near Field Multibeam Antenna, together with their associated circuitry, are compared in the case of a Ku-band communication satellite covering Western Europe. For both configurations an active antenna solution with a multiple beam type coverage is assumed.

articleTitle: Finite ground plane effects on the radiation patterns of a rectangular microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Microstrip antennas are popular for their low profile and light weight. They have been analyzed using a number of analytical and numerical techniques [1-3]. Most of the investigations have been based on antennas with infinitely large ground planes. Microstrip antennas may, however, be applied with finite ground plane in some cases such as feed elements in reflector antennas. In such cases, the radiation characteristics of the microstrip antennas with finite ground plane is very important in order to predict the performance of the reflector antenna. Moreover, from the practical point of view, the dimensions of the ground plane of a commercial antenna cannot be made infinitely large, and therefore the knowledge of radiation characteristics with finite ground plane is very important to an antenna designer.

articleTitle: Multiple scattering of electromagnetic waves by N conducting strips
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The problem of multiple scattering of a plane wave or a line source field by a planar array of parallel conducting strips is addressed. Two methods of solution are presented for each type of excitation. The first method is rigorous and based on the boundary value approach while the second is asymptotic and based on the Karp-Russek technique. One of the important applications of this problem is the simulation of cylindrical reflector antenna surfaces by N strips. Therefore, both methods are used to compute the echo width patterns for different configurations of strips due to plane wave incidence and the far field patterns of simulated cylindrical reflectors due to line source excitation. Comparison between patterns of simulated and solid cylindrical reflectors is presented to illustrate the validity of simulation.

articleTitle: Design and analysis op multi-shell spherical microwave lens antennas
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Spherical dielectric lenses are a viable consideration in many antenna systems but have not been used extensively since the I960's. The most attractive characteristic of spherical lenses is their inherent symmetry, which permits the formation of beams in any direction without scan loss. Also, because several beams can be supported simultaneously and the focusing properties are independent of frequency, spherically symmetric lenses can be used in a broad spectrum of antenna systems. Most of the previous analysis and design work in this area has been limited in its coverage, having been performed before the advent of sophisticated computers.

articleTitle: Analysis of intermodulations in microwave amplifiers by frequency domain harmonic balancing
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper introduces a harmonic balance technique in the frequency domain for efficiently determining the harmonic and intermodulation products of nonlinear networks with multi-tone inputs. This eliminates the solution of the system equations in the time domain, conversion from the time domain to the frequency domain (discrete Fourier transform) and reconstruction of the port voltage time domain waveforms from their Fourier series coeffficients as performed in the standard harmonic balance [1],[2],[3].

articleTitle: A new computational approach to solve the self-consistent GTTD formulation
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: For avoiding mathematical complexity occuring in the 2-dimensional exterior scattering problems, which consists of an infinitely-long perfectly-conducting convex cylinder illuminated by a source of current filament, either electric or magnetic, near the cylinder, N. Wang [1] proposed a self-consistent GTD formulation. The latter avers that, if the 2-dimensional problem is concerned with, the convex surface may be alternatively modeled to be composed of flat planes linking with wedges of finite number, then the original convex surface diffraction problem is transformed into an one of just considering the wedge diffraction and geometrical optic field calculation, refer to Fig. 1. Moreover a matrix with sparse manner is always resulted in the self-consistent GTD formulation, fortunately, due to the specially inbred characteristics of the constituent in this matrix, the Gauss-Seidel iterative method may be applied to solve this formulation very effectively since the convergence condition is well satisfied.

articleTitle: Application of equivalent EDGE currents in radar cross section calculations
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The basic principle of Equivalent Edge Currents (EEC) theory states that an asymptotic approximation to the scattered field or part thereof can be found by integrating hypothetical line currents placed along the edge of the scattering body [1], Since the derivation of EEC has been approached by a number of authors, different types and versions of these currents have emerged. Two types of EEC exist; these produce different parts of the scattered field. For each type, two versions exist; first version EEC are theoretically limited to be applied at caustics, whereas EEC of the second version are applicable for all field points. See section 2. A detailed comparative study of the different types and versions is given in [2].

articleTitle: Input admittance of an infinitely long insulated antenna excited across a wide feed GAP
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Expressions are derived for the input admittance and aperture electromagnetic fields in the feed gap of a solid insulated antenna with infinite extension. This is done by solving the boundary value problem where the fields are represented by Fourier series built up by superposition of basic sets of φ-independent cylindrical waves. Such waves are obtained from the solution of the Helmholtz equation governing the z-directed electric Hertzian potential. The axial aperture electric field in the gap is in the form of a Fourier Bessel series aad used to find the input admittance. Results are represented for the aperture fields and input admittances at different radii and gap widths.

articleTitle: A horizontal oscillating magnetic dipole over a lossy ground
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The radiation field of a horizontal magnetic dipole located above a homogeneous lossy ground is formulated using the dyadic Green's functions. The resulting field vectors are then split into the primary and secondary components. The primary components represent those that would exist in the absence of the ground leaving the secondary components to represent the contribution of the ground. For different frequencies and various ground conductivities, the secondary field components are determined and compared with the primary ones. The results indicate that the magnitudes of the secondary electric field components are as large as the corresponding primary ones, but are nearly out of phase, in particular when the field point moves towards the air-earth interface and inside the earth. On the other hand, the earth influence on the magnetic field components increases with both the frequency and earth conductivity.

articleTitle: A slot-coupled circularly polarized microstrip antenna for dual-frequency use
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Recently, an active phased array antenna using monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) and digital signal processing techniques is being investigated to obtain advanced function including electrically beam scanning and adaptive pattern control for eliminating interference signals. Trials to develop a compact-size, light-weight and low-profile antenna for satellite mobile communications using such an active phased array have been reported<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1)(2)</sup>. To realize the active array antenna for satellite mobile communications, it will be important to develop an element antenna and active components suitable for monolithic and integrated structures. In addition, techniques for multi-layered feed network are required.

articleTitle: Derivation of the diffraction coefficients related to a cylindrically curved metallic sheet from the surface currents
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The diffraction of high-frequency waves by the edges of curved sheets is an important topic which finds several applications in the reflector antennas theory as well as in radar scattering investigations. The most effective methods to analyse such phenomena are the Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (GTD) and the Physical Theory of Diffraction (PTD) For the application of the former some coefficients (diffraction coefficients of different kinds, attenuation constants, divergence factors, etc) play basic role while the use of PTD requires the knowledge of explicit expressions for the induced surface currents. According to Ufimtsev's PTD [1] the total induced surface current J can be represented as the sum of two components, one the physical optics current J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and the other J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, a correction to J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> due to all other effects not included in physical optics: J = J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> + J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> The correction term J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> is due to perturbations created by the departure of the surface from an infinite plane and may arise, for example, from the curvature of the surface at a shadow boundary or from geometrical discontinuities such as edges.

articleTitle: Theory of multiply fed/loaded dipole antenna with finite internal impedance
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A Wiener-Hopf type analysis is introduced to determine the radiation characteristics of an imperfectly conducting multiply fed/loaded solid dipole antenna. The analysis is applicable to dipoles with constant impedance per unit length. Expressions for the input admittance and current distribution are presented in terms of the imposed electric fields along the antenna length. Such imposed fields can be caused by voltage feeds, active loading and/or passive loading. Very good agreement is observed when comparison is made with available experimental and analytical data show.

articleTitle: A high resolution step-scan technique for low sidelobe phased array antennas
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The basic principle of granularity of beam positions in phased array antennas is considered. It is shown that by adjusting the phase distribution of central elements a fine incremental step between adjacent beam positions can be obtained. The effect of adjusting the phase distribution of central or edge elements on the sidelobe level is also studied. For a given beam position, the variation of the phase for edge elements has more severe effect on the sidelobe level than that of central elements.

articleTitle: Stacked patch elements for spacecraft feed arrays
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Geostationary satellites providing services in the UHF and lower microwave bands have been proposed which use large deployable reflectors with array feeds to form several simultaneous beams. If conventional horn antennas are used in such a feed the mass and volume may be excessive.

articleTitle: A symmetrical node for the FD-TD method
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The Finite Difference Time Domain (FD-TD) method based on Yee's algorithm has been used intensively in the past few years to solve electromagnetic scattering/radiation [1]-[3] and eigenvalue problems [4]. In order to provide second order accuracy, Yee's lattice requires that the mesh on which the electric field components and the permittivity are defined, be interspaced with the mesh on which the magnetic field components and the permeability are defined.

articleTitle: Considerations to increase the isolation between two antennas kept side by side
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: CW or FM CW radar performance is dependant on the isolation between the transmitter and receiver. The sensitivity of FM-CW radar is limited by the noise accompanying the transmitter signal which leaks into the receiver. Although advances have been made in reducing the AM and FM noise generated by high power CW transmitters, the noise is usually of sufficient magnitude compared with the echo signal to require some means of minimizing the leakage that finds its way into the receiver. Separate antennas and direct cancellation of the leakage singal are two techniques which give considerable isolation between transmitter and receiver [1]. When two separate antennas are used for transmitting and receiving, isolation between them is a very important factor to improve the performance of a CW or FM CW radar. Achieving the proper isolation between the transmitting and receving antennas is a difficult task, if they have to be placed closely due to space contracts.

articleTitle: Scanning properties of circularly polarized microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A microstrip patch antenna has a simple geometry which is normally etched on a dielectric substrate to form a resonant cavity over the ground plane. Depending on the size of the patch various TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mn</inf> modes resonate in the cavity and the radiation occurs due to the fringing field at the patch edge. Because they are highly resonant structures their bandwidth is small and operation in a wider band or multiple bands can be achieved by stacking several units. In the past, they were usually used for operation in the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode to generate a radiation in the broadside direction. The circular polarization is also possible, which can be achieved either by feeding the element at two angular positions separated by Δθ = π/2n, where n is the index of the mode in the azimuthal direction, or by a patch surface deformation to generate two orthogonal modes at phase quadrature. The operation of microstrip antennas simultaneously in several modes provides a unique scanning property that can be used in array designs. It provides a number of important features and the most useful ones are: 1) the array beam can be scanned readily by introducing phase shifts between different modes, 2) the antenna beam can be shaped arbitrarily, and 3) they can be designed to generate a null behind the scanned beam. The latter property can be used to eliminate the grating lobes in highly scanned arrays or, to reduce the number of array elements without generating a grating lobe. Multimode operation with microstrip antennas is feasible, since they can be stacked easily. In the following sections initially an approximate analysis is provided to show the scanning property and then a few computed and measured results are presented, using the first few resonant modes.

articleTitle: Analytic solution for electromagnetic scattering by spheroids with non-parallel axes
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: By expanding the incident and scattered electric fields in terms of an appropriate set of vector spheroidal eigenfunctions, an exact solution is obtained to the problem of scattering of a plane electromagnetic wave by two perfectly conducting prolate spheroids of arbitrary orientation. The boundary conditions are imposed by expressing the field scattered by one spheroid in terms of the spheroidal coordinates attached to the other spheroid, using the rotational-translational addition theorems for vector spheroidal wave functions. The column matrix of the scattered field expansion coefficients is equal to the product of a square matrix, which is independent of the direction and polarization of the incident wave, and the column matrix of the known incident field expansion coefficients. The solution of the associated set of simultaneous linear equations gives the unknown scattered field expansion coefficients, from which one can determine the electromagnetic field at any point in space.

articleTitle: A time domain approach for determining ground impedance on printed circuit boards
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Starting with a frequency domain analysis of the ground impedance between two points on a solid ground plane of a printed circuit board, closed formulae to calculate the ground impedance in frequency domain is presented. The approach which takes into account the skin-effect and striction effect in frequency domain is extended to calculate the voltage difference between two points on the ground plane in time domain. The time domain approach takes into account the transient skin-effect and transient striction effect which become important in the case of designing high speed printed circuits boards or back planes.

articleTitle: Computer-aided design of broadband non-uniform fin-line couplers for millimetre-wave applications
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Analysis and design of a broadband fin-line coupler using non-uniform slot spacing is described. Results, both analytical and experimental, show the viability of this type of coupler at millimetre-wave frequencies.

articleTitle: An exact electromagnetic field theory for the broadband h-plane waveguide junction circulator
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Waveguide y-junction circulator in a microwave ferrite device whose structure is simple and whose size is small. It finds many applications. It is especially broadband. There is a metal step in such circulators to reduce junction height and to obtain the necessary impedance transformation. In 1975 Helszajn stated how to obtain a n=2 Chebyehev response characteristics with such junctions [1]. But his treatment did not base on the electromagnetic field boundary value solution. In 1978 Akaiwa analysed a similar structure by electromagnetic field theory. But his computation did not show the n=2 Chebyehev response characteristics appearing in experiments [2]. It is necessary to study further such junction circulator. The structure to be studied is shown in Fig. 1.

articleTitle: Millimetre-wave radiometer systems: Principle and applications
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, the principle of millimetre wave radiometer systems, their applications, and future trends will be presented with more detailed descriptions on two radiometers recently developed at MPB Technologies Inc. The following is an outline of the paper.

articleTitle: Calculation of transmission line parameters with the boundary element method
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The objective of this paper is to demonstrate the efficient calculation of design parameters using the boundary element method coupled with a highly interactive package for entering the transmission line configuration. The geometry of the problem that can be solved is arbitrary. Conductors lay be infinitesimally thin or may be of finite area. As well, the conductors may be embedded in one or acre dielectric materials.

articleTitle: Offset rectangular multilayer microstrip antennas: Theory and experiments
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A study of stacked microstrip antennas with an offset radiating element structure is presented. These structures ore investigated both theoretically and experimentally. The theory takes into account higher modes caused by the offset.

articleTitle: Properties and novel fabrication methods of opto-electronic waveguides
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: There are numerous materials and techniques for the fabrication of optical waveguides and opto-electronic circuits, however all structures require knowledge of the guiding properties for the realization of practical devices. We have studied in detail the guiding properties of the planar thin film waveguide, from the most basic, three-layer structure to multilayer waveguides. In sections II and III we describe general formulas for the field distributions, the eigenvalue equations from which the propagation constant can be found, and the generalized dispersion properties, which tell us the variation in effective index with respect to any physical parameter upon which the refractive index or thickness of any layer may depend.

articleTitle: Design study of a vertically-polarized radar antenna
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The objective of this study was to design a receive only, vertically-polarized marine X-Band radar antenna with the following specifications: Frequency of operation: 9.4 GHz Horizontal beamwidth: 1.0 degrees Vertical beamwidth: 20 degrees Maximum horizontal aperture: 10 feet Gain: 30 dB Horizontal sidelobes: less than 30 dB Bandwidth: 1.5 percent or 150 MHz The design study was to yield an antenna with a small physical cross-section which might be combined with an existing horizontally-polarized antenna in a single housing. In addition to having a maximum length of 10 feet, the antenna aperture was to be a maximum of a foot high and only a few inches deep. A design study of the antenna architecture was carried out based on microstrip phased array antenna technology. CAD software was developed for designing the array elements, as well as the complete phased array. Subcomponents of the antenna, such as the microstrip elements, 4-by-4 subarray, combiners and corporate feed structures, were built and measurements were carried out to validate the design studies.

articleTitle: GPS antenna selection: Preliminary range and field test results
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The omni directional antennas currently used with Global Positioning System (GPS) receivers can contribute significant errors, particularly when used in high accuracy measurements. Some GPS experiments require signals to be detected with less than 2 degrees of phase error, and with less than 0.1 nanosecond delay error. Antennas must be capable of tracking signals at two L-band frequencies, from multiple satellites, at all elevations above 15 degrees. This paper describes a study by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), and by the University of New Brunswick (UNB), to select antenna/backplane configurations with low levels of multipath, and to calibrate the variation of antenna phase delay as a function of observing angle. Measurements of candidate antennas are underway at an antenna range and in field tests.

articleTitle: A Representation of the quasi-stationary boundary condition for the magnetic field density
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The paper develops an explicit formula for the surface current on the basis of self-consistent field and current investigation at an interface of two different media. The concept of the transverse-longitudinal decomposition of an arbitrary field within a homogeneous medium is used to achieve the purpose.

articleTitle: Frequency perturbation for circular array of coupled cylindrical dipole antennas
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents a procedure for calculating efficiently the frequency perturbations for circular array of coupled cylindrical dipole antenna. This is commonly done through subsequent application of the algorithm at different values of frequency. A novel technique is developed where the coupled integral equations for the circular array is solved using the method of moments at a single frequency. Then Taylor series expansion is built up for the current distribution over each element of the array as a function of frequency. The derivatives needed in the expansion are calculated without repeated calculation of the impedance matrix or its inverse; hence, saving computer time, storage and efforts. Convergence is guaranteed by extracting out the poles or by expanding the inverse of the current distributions on each antenna element. Pocklington integral equation is suggested. Kernel singularity is overcome using extended boundary condition [1,2] resulting in a regular kernel. Current expansion basis of the entire domain type is chosen to save computer storage. The increase in the expected time needed to carry out such integration numerically is overcome by a semianalytic technique. This is done by expanding the kernel in Fourier series. Infinite Fourier series (IFS) is chosen for the self kernel, while finite Fourier series (FFS) is used for the mutual kernel. This is because the self kernel is a bad behaved function, while the mutual kernel is a well-behaved one. The method of feeding suggested is a particularly appropriate method which represents the electric field distribution in the aperture of a coaxial fed monopole over a ground plane [3].

articleTitle: Transient response of a circular cylinder to an impulsive cylindrical wave
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An analytical study of the early-time surface current density induced on a perfectly conducting circular cylinder excited by a parallel line source carrying a δ-function current has been carried out. Expressions of the current density for both the shadow and the illuminated region are obtained. Numerical results are presented to illustrate the variation of the surface current density with time for two different locations of the line source with respect to the cylinder.

articleTitle: An impressed field modeling on a linear antenna
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Antenna radiative pattern and input impedance are related to the antenna current distribution. The latter, in turn, is determined by the distribution of an impressed (external) electric field on the antenna surface. Therefore, the proper description of the distribution of the impressed electric field on the antenna surface is the important starting point in a theoretical discussion of antenna problems. This paper, in particular, considers the distribution of an impressed field on a radiating linear' cylindrical antenna driven from a gap. Consider the cylindrical antenna (Fig. 1) of the radius ρ. The antenna is driven from the gap of a width w. The driving electric field E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sup> on the gap is parallel to the antenna surface and does not depend on azimuth φ, i.e. E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> = E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> = 0; E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf> = E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sup>(z); |z| < w/2 (1).

articleTitle: Design theory of circular polarization radial line slot array antenna
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A radial power divider which used for feed system in the phased array antenna will decrease the size of antenna and reduce feed loss [1] [2]. For the satellite communication and satellite broadcast, there is an increasing interest in circular polarization high efficiency planar antenna. MAKOTO ANTO et al. suggested a radial line slot antenna. This paper will give the design theory of such antenna.

articleTitle: Secondary diffraction of a plane wave by a two-part impedance strip
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The scattering of high-frequency waves by two-part impedance strips is an important topic in diffraction theory because it can provide usefull information concerning the radiation of electromagnetic waves in the presence of discontinuity in the material properties of a surface of finite width, as well as of composite structures on aircrafts, satellites etc. According to the Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (GTD) the primary diffracted fields from a two-part impedance strip can be evaluated easily by using the known canonical solutions related both to an impedance half-plane and to a two-part impedance plane.

articleTitle: A single-wire spiral antenna with a small ground plane
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A single-wire spiral antenna backed by a small ground plane is proposed as an element which is capable of radiating a circularly polarized wave. The current distribution of the antenna element and the ground plane is numerically analyzed using the moment method. On the basis of the current distribution, the radiation characteristics are evaluated.

articleTitle: An effective method for phase-only nulling
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Several methods for array pattern nulling with control of phase-only are discussed in some papers. Now, a more effective method for phase-only nulling is proposed in this paper. It is seen that the method of calculating the phases for minimized weight perturbation in the least square sense is given, with attention focused on the computation of the beam space coefficients.

articleTitle: Time domain analysis of the transient electromagnetic measurement system
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The transient eleotromagnetio measurement system is useful for obtaining the time-domain transient responses. Short pulse, wide-bandwidth and compact range, all of these have made the transient measurement significantly distinct from the conventional frequency domain or CW measurement.

articleTitle: A new closed formula for inductance in microstrip step in width discontinuity
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In recents years the development of CAD systems for microwave circuits design requests very accurate and efficient models for microwave elements and discontinuities. In this paper a new accurate and efficient formula for the inductance in the equivalent circuit of microstrip step in width discontinuity is presented. The comparison with previous formulas and experimental results shows good agreement with the literature.

articleTitle: A new broadband miniature helical dipole
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A new type of broadband miniature antenna consists of helical dipole folded by central conductor is presented in this paper. Besides a brief analysis, the experimental results show the good performances of wider bandwidth (25%–40%), higher input impedance(about 200 Ohms), and flexible for designing, it is suitable to be used as both mobile vertical antenna and excitor of Yagi antenna.

articleTitle: Coupled microstrip antennas for wider bandwidth
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Narrow bandwidth available from microstrip patch radiators has been recognized as the most significant factor limiting the applications of this class of antennas. Different approaches for increasing the bandwidth available from microstrip antennas include: i) use of thicker substrates with low ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> [1], (ii) use of multiple patches in one plane [2], (iii) use of multiple patches stacked vertically [3], and (iv) use of broadband impedance matching networks [4], One of the configurations [2] in the group (ii) makes use of rectangular patches gap-coupled along the non-radiating edges. This particular configuration appears very attractive as the layout can be made compact [5] thus avoiding the use of large substrate area and consequential degradation in radiation pattern over the operating frequency range.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of curved microstrip line antennas
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The microstrip Green's function of a horizontal dipole is employed for formulating an integral equation for the current distribution along the arbitrary shape microstrip line antenna. The resulting integral equation is then solved for calculating the current distribution using a moment method. Analytical expressions for the far zone fields are obtained using an asymptotic method for evaluating the sommerfeld integrals. Examples illustrating the accuracy of the method and characteristics of selected printed antennas are presented. It is found that for undulated printed line elements, the resonance length increases by increasing the undulation height. Various examples of undulated printed line elements which are useful for array design are investigated. The effect of the undulation height on the radiation characteristics of the printed line is also studied.

articleTitle: Scattering by a rough surface modelled as parallel conducting cylinders partially buried into a ground plane
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The problem of bistatic scattering from a rough surface modelled as a regular or random arrangement of infinitely long perfectly conducting circular cylinders that are partially buriedinto a ground plane is studied with the help of the image principle. The solution for a single cylinder is obtained first for both the transverse magnetic (TM) and the transverse electric (TE) polarizations of the obliquely incident plane wave. The method of approach is based on the representation of the incident field, the specularly reflected field from the ground plane and the scattered fields from the cylinder and its image in the ground plane due to the image of the incident plane wave in terms of cylindrical vector wave functions. These wave functions satisfy the vector Helmholz equation and the Sommerfeld radiation condition at infinity. By imposing the boundary conditions on the surface of the cylinder, an infinite system of equations for the even and odd mode expansion coefficients of the scattered field is obtained. These equations are solved numerically for small and moderate size cylinders in the resonance region. The single cylinder solution is later incorporated into an equivalent Twersky model to obtain the results like the generalized reflection coefficient, the bistatic crosssection for the rough surface.

articleTitle: High speed opto-electronic devices with applications in optical ranging and signal processing
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Very fast response times can be obtained from optical sources and detectors based on a semiconductor diode technology in appropriate materials. For example, detectors with a response in the visible and near-infrared regions can be fabricated in silicon, germanium or III-V alloy semiconductors with response times measured on a picosecond timescale. Diode laser sources can be produced from III-V alloy semiconductors, such as (Ga, In)As, with commensurate response times. Commercially available pulsed laser diode sources have pulse lengths down to several tens of picoseconds; diode detectors are available with a pulse response in the same range. These devices are being utilised in an increasingly wide variety of applications which exploit the capability of making time measurements on a picosecond timescale or, in the frequency domain, of responding to signals in the 1–10 GHz region. In what follows, two specific applications are discussed. The first exploits the picosecond timing capability to generate an optical ranging system with millimetre-scale distance resolution. The second is concerned with the use of high speed optical signal processing techniques to generate the microwave drive signals for a phased array radar antenna.

articleTitle: Analysis of multiple-step discontinuities in rectangular waveguides
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The equivalence principle and the moment method which was previously employed in the solution of single-step waveguide discontinuities, is extended to solve for the field and the scattering matrix coefficients at the junctions of multiple-step discontinuities. Scattering matrix coefficients are computed for representative double-step discontinuities and frequencies. The method is simple and straightforward, and the results obtained are compared with data available in the literature.

articleTitle: Impedance characteristics of circular microstrip patches
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Microstrip antennas are highly resonant structures and, for simple patch configurations, the bandwidths of each mode is quite small. As an antenna, their most useful mode is the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode that radiates in the broadside direction with a good gain. All other modes, TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nm</inf>, radiate conical beams with a null in the broadside and have a pattern peak that moves towards the endfire direction by increasing the mode index η (in the azimuthal direction). These antennas are normally excited by using a feeding probe from a coaxial line, or a co-planar transmission line. The excitation coefficient of different modes depend on their proximity to the resonance mode and the location of the feed. When only one mode must be excited, the feed configuration or its location must be optimized to eliminate the excitation of other modes.

articleTitle: Circularly polarized microstrip line antennas
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The analysis of an arbitrary shape printed loop microstrip antenna is presented. The Green's function of the microstrip antenna is employed for formulating an integral equation for the current distribution on the printed loop which is then solved using a moment method. Design of various loop shapes for producing circularly polarized field will be presented.

articleTitle: Characteristics of a centered-inclined slot coupler for waveguide-fed slot arrays
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Waveguide fed planar slot arrays employ resonant slots to couple power from the main waveguide to crossed branch waveguides A centered-inclined slot located on the common broad wall is the most widely used coupling slot. Power coupled into the branch waveguide is controlled by the magnitude of the tilt angle, θ with respect to the longitudinal axis of the main line.

articleTitle: Some considerations on mutual coupling of microstrip phased array
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In designing a microstrip phased array (MSA-array) shown in Fig.1, it is important to estimate the influence of mutual coupling between microstrip antennas(MSA)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1)</sup>. In this paper, we investigate the effect of mutual coupling on the radiation pattern of the antenna. After calculating the coupling, the experimental patterns are compared to the calculated ones. From these results, it is shown that the experimental patterns agree well with the theoretical ones considering the mutual coupling of the antenna.

articleTitle: Wideband stacked microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: To increase the bandwidth of a microstrip antenna, while providing it with a protective outer layer, a structure comprised of two or three stacked radiating elements with several dielectric layers can be employed [1]. The focus of this paper is a method developed to compute the geometric parameters of this type of antenna, coaxially fed, containing up to three stacked conductors and dielectrics. This method involves computing, in the spectral domain, the necessary Green's functions, then determining the currents using an integral equation solved by a method of moments. From the radiator surface current values, we deduce the antenna's principal characteristics: input impedance, radiation pattern, etc. This method enabled determination of the geometric parameters of an antenna with two square, centered radiating elements and a protective layer. The theoretical and experimental results obtained around 1.6 GHz and 11 GHz are very encouraging. The differences between the theoretical and measured curves can be attributed to an insufficient number of modes in the description of the current.

articleTitle: Plane wave diffraction by a superelliptical aperture
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Recently, the elliptical aperture has been introduced in parabolic reflector antenna applications to supplement conventional circular and rectangular apertures [1]. Since these three apertures and a continuum of others are all comprised by the superelliptical aperture, an investigation of the latter yields results of great generality. Furthermore, whereas the circle is geometrically characterized by one parameter and the ellipse and the rectangle by two, the introduction of the superellipse provides the antenna designer with three adjustable parameters.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of short/thick solid antenna with finite feed GAP
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Expressions are presented for the input admittance and the current distribution along a linear antenna without restrictions on either the length or the thickness. These expressions which are based on Hurd's Wiener-Hopf type analysis, are used to find the characteristics of short as well as thick antennas. It is found that although using one term of the solution asymptotic series produces accurate results for thick antennas, more series terms have to be used when the antenna is thin.

articleTitle: On the electromagnetic response of an imperfectly conducting object to a current loop in the presence of a lossy ground
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An approximate numerical method is developed to determine the electromagnetic wave scattering by imperfectly conducting objects located inside a lossy ground. The incident field of the exciting loop, which is located above the ground, is determined using the dyadic Green's functions for a half-space. The scattering problem is then formulated using the magnetic field integral equation of an unbounded region, but keeping the incident field of the half-space. The method of moment is used to reduce the integral equation to a matrix one to determine the induced surface currents on the object's surface. The Surface currents of the object represent a set of electric and magnetic dipoles distributed tangentially on the object. The dyadic Green's functions of the half-space are again used to compute the scattered field from the object, which is due to the electric and magnetic dipoles with their appropriate amplitude distributions. Representative numerical data for a range of source frequencies, object dimensions and depths of burial are presented.

articleTitle: An improved zig-zag antenna with higher gain-bandwidth product
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A conventional symmetric Zig-zag antenna is improved by adding a shunt shaped dipole at the feeding terminals or a shaped dipole as parasitic reflector, this dipole results in an increment of radiated gain in forward direction while remaining the wider frequency bandwidth of Zig-zag antenna. By means of the method of moments with piecewise-sine bases and Galerkin's procedure, the Zig-zag structure and the shaped dipole are analysed separately then integratively. The former result provides a reasonable selection for the initial data of optimized parameters, and the latter is to be a subroutine of the optimization program. The simplex method is used to optimize the geometric sizes of antenna for the object of both higher gain and wider frequency bandwidth. A typical sample of the improved Zig-zag antenna with three peroids is designed for the maximum gain of 9.5 dB, VSWR ≤ 1.6, relative frequency bandwidth ≥15% at 1300 MHz which have been verified by the experimental data.

articleTitle: Wave propagation and current distribution for a conductor impinging on a lossy interface
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The study of wave propagation along conductors located at or near a lossy planar interface is of interest in geoelectromagnetics for remote sensing applications as well as in the power engineering field for transmission line analysis. It is important to determine the effect of the interface on the propagation and radiation characteristics of the geometry, especially if it is highly lossy as in the case of the earth. In the past, almost all theories have treated the problem assuming a thin wire approximation to model the conductor. This means only axially directed currents having a uniform azimuthal distribution are assumed to propagate. Various solutions to this simplified problem have been presented in past decades and even this task has proven difficult; beginning with Carson in 1926 [1] who took an approximate circuit approach, to Wait [2] who presented an exact solution in integral form. All this work, based on the thin wire approximation, has been successfully applied to many practical problems. However, if the conductor is not thin or is located near the interface, the azimuthal current distribution will not be uniform and azimuthal current components will also be present.

articleTitle: Effect of feed GAP width on the impedance of biconical antennas
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The biconical antenna fed across a wide feed gap is studied as a boundary value problem using modal analysts. The study deals with finite length antennas, and considers two limiting cases of biconical antenna angles i.e. wide angle (spherical antennas) and very small angle (thin wire antennas). Expressions for the input and apparent terminal admittances are derived and corresponding values compared with data in available literature (with delta function generator).

articleTitle: Electromagnetic response of a two-layer dielectric spherical object in the field of a dipole source
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The electromagnetic response of an arbitrarily polarized dipole source in the vicinity of a two-layer dielectric spherical object in a lossy medium is investigated analytically. A technique based on the dyadic Green's functions is employed to determine the fields in every region. The formulation can be applied to a wide variety of electromagnetic sources. Numerical results are presented in the near field zone and at low frequencies to determine the effect of the coating on the scattered field and the influence of the coating on the degree of detectability of a coated object.

articleTitle: The effects of phased-array antennas on the performance of wideband LFM radars
publicationTitle: 1988 Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In many modern applications, radars are required to detect and track multiple targets at long ranges with very good range and angle accuracy The combination of these requirements can be met by the use of high transmitter power, wideband linear frequency modulated (LFM) waveforms, and electrically large phased-array antennas.
